core_obligations: Choose a filtration with cyclic prime quotients and use the earlier result identifying the minimal primes of the support with the minimal primes of the primes occurring in the filtration (proof lines 15418-15421).

Compare the associated primes with the support: an associated prime contains a minimal prime of the support, and conversely a minimal prime of the support is associated, so the two sets of minimal primes coincide (proof lines 15423-15447).
proof_roadmap: Identify the first and third sets through a filtration (proof lines 15418-15421).
Relate associated primes to the support and compare minimal ones (proof lines 15423-15448).
difficulty_reason: The proposition states that for a finite module over a Noetherian ring three sets of primes coincide: the minimal primes in the support, the minimal primes among the associated primes, and the minimal primes occurring in any filtration with cyclic prime quotients (statement lines 15404-15416). The proof does not use primary decomposition: it reads the first and third sets off a filtration, then relates associated primes to the support by annihilator arguments and compares the minimal elements of the two sets (proof lines 15418-15448). Transferring minimality between the two descriptions is the step that closes the comparison. H2.
